scope: Offline B1 text with German and English meanings. Final sign-off by separate Codex readers.

lessonsRead.observation: Sauna gives the porridge habit its past frame; the learner still likes porridge but usually hurries to work. The breakfast contrast and frequency are clear in both translations. The root cues use English grammar labels, as in the specification’s example.
The move gives the former and current cooking habits a time frame. The closure question motivates the egg example; the repeated activity makes magluto intelligible.
The distance answer names one kilometre. Karon and sagad carry different functions, and the whole habitual verb is recoverable with the supplied root.
The occasional beach visit contrasts with usually resting at home. The second reply answers who comes along. Both glosses convey being alone most of the time.
Night shift versus day shift explains changed sleep. The hours answer makes the frequency concrete and both translations support the whole habitual verb.
Midnight biscuits give way to hot tea. Batasan and gibiyaan express the former habit and its end. The additional example introduces becoming accustomed to the replacement.

The learner’s present ability to walk outside contrasts with staying indoors in the early months. The question anchors sauna; matag directly modifies hapon. The previous Apan option was removed; Tali sa cannot introduce magpabilin.
The old gym routine is replaced by yoga. The reply gives an early work schedule as the reason. Matag fits directly before buntag among the four visible choices.
The changed town has more vehicles; the former square is now a parking lot. Matag hapon times the recurring games, and apan contrasts the two uses of the square.
The festival retains its food despite changed music. The closing reply contrasts a former dancing habit with wala na mi magsayaw. Both translations preserve that cessation.
The grandmother receives a direct three-role answer without learner-side gihapon or kada. Both new bases now naturally explain hurrying to work.
The friend hears eggs then vegetables, with a past habit, sagad and the constrained transition to karon. The younger speaker's cooking and the transfer's drink example agree.
The coworker's distance is now practised as a habitual kilometre walk with Karon/sagad/maglakaw; the early learner no longer produces matag.
The neighbour learns a cousin sometimes joins and usually the learner goes alone. Usahay, mouban and the contrast serve three different roles.
The host's old shifts lead to an elliptical formerly-little vs now-eight-hours sleep contrast. Matulog is appropriately cued against completed forms; permi supplies frequency.
The friend's replacement tea habit is distinguished from the old snack by Karon and a clean bank, then permi and cued moinom. The naandan transfer provides the L7 foundation.

The tutor asks about the first months, which selects Sauna rather than Karon. Tali sa cannot introduce magpabilin ko and Ngano would ask an irrelevant question. The habituated response and its two remaining blanks align with the prior present-day contrast.
The cousin gets a clear early-work rationale for switching to yoga. The revised temporal bank, work form and every-morning frequency each have a single contextual answer.
The barber's lost quiet square is now a parking area, an appropriate new detail. Matag, the former play habit and the contrast are each tested.

The elder asks Mao ra ba gihapon ...?, keeping reinforcement on the recognition side. The learner contrasts Lahi na with mao ra, and the three final cloze roles and their alternatives are now aligned.
The grandmother hears rice porridge contrasted with bread and asks whether the learner still likes it. The learner explains the time pressure; kada is actively recalled too early.
The friend asks about cooking when the eatery closed; a preceding sauna licenses habitual magluto with past German/English. Both patterns contrast buying with cooking.
The coworker's jeepney and walking commute leads to a real question about distance. The final reply tests distance and late-stage matag but no habitual form.
The neighbour asks who comes to the beach, then hears 'my neighbour' without identifying a different neighbour. The choice of optional companion could be clearer.
The host asks about old shifts and current sleep. Night/day works, but the follow-up tests ability and early matag instead of the block's frequency and a habitual action.
The friend learns midnight biscuits were dropped in favour of tea. Wala na ko mag- appears here in advance of its productive block.
The tutor asks about heat and the first months after moving. Naandan, sauna and staying inside contrast clearly; the transfer applies acclimatization to traffic noise.
The cousin hears gym versus yoga and asks why yoga suits the learner. The last reply explains home practice but the cloze tests ability and size rather than habit and frequency.
The barber gets increased traffic and a quiet square as local contrasts. The third turn's expression for 'what do you miss?' requires a target for the thing missed.
The elder asks about fiesta music, food and dancing. The learner produces recognition-only gihapon and the speech task selects no connector/aspect anchor.

findings.issue: L1 teaches, requires and blanks kada + time, which the architect explicitly reserves for recognition in them-lines. The same answer also produces gihapon. Matag is a productive learner answer at L3/L5 and appears in the L1 transfer, ahead of its L7–10 block. L2's cloze tests L4–6 usahay; L6 teaches the L7–10 wala na ko mag- as its first learner line.
findings.recommendation: Use the block's productive items in the learner/cloze/transfer slots. Keep kada and recognition-only reinforcement on partner turns. Stage matag and discontinued wala na + base in L7–10.

findings.issue: The P8 design specifies frequency, a whole habitual/completed form with a same-root aspect contrast, and sauna/karon/apan. Nearly every lesson drops the connector or frequency role; L3/L5 have no form, L8 tests ability plus size and L9 an adjective. Several form banks lack the corresponding ni- form. Even L1 tags apan as a choice.
findings.recommendation: Build the three roles into each natural final reply with distinct valid choices and a meaningful habitual/completed contrast. Set frequency to choice, temporal/contrast slot to connector, and supply an aspect cue on the form.

findings.issue: The person asking is your neighbour, and you identify the companion only as 'my neighbour', leaving it unclear whether you mean your listener or somebody else.
findings.recommendation: Give the companion a distinct natural referent such as a cousin, sibling or named neighbour.

findings.issue: Naandan na nako is scheduled for L4–6 but is first practiced at L7. The L7 trophy is correct; the missing foundation is earlier.
findings.recommendation: Introduce it naturally in a preceding transfer or reply, for example about getting used to tea instead of snacks, without moving the L7 trophy.

findings.issue: Unsa may imong gimingaw gikan sa una? uses the experiencer form gimingaw with imong instead of identifying what is missed, and gikan sa una reads literally as 'from the beginning'.
findings.recommendation: Use an idiomatic form such as Unsa may imong gimingawan sa lungsod sauna? Keep dialogue[3] as the experiencer's Gimingaw ko sa ... answer.

findings.issue: The learner is explicitly taught and asked to speak pareho gihapon, although gihapon reinforcement is recognition-only in L7–10; lahi/musika/pareho are two predicates and a noun, with no connector/aspect-bearing word. Recall also allows 'Lahi na ang porma sa pista karon' meaning the form of the fiesta changed, plausible after an open question about the fiesta.
findings.recommendation: Keep this beat by expressing food continuity without learner-side gihapon, move gihapon to the elder if desired, choose apan or another valid anchor, and replace porma with an unworkable alternative.

lessonsRead.observation: Sauna + mokaon habitual with apan karon contrast is correct and matches the beat; youOne 14 words, tokens and chunks valid. youTwo uses 'kada buntag' productively and clozes it although 'kada + time unit' is recognition-only for lessons 1-3; replaced with 'inig buntag' (already used in L7 learner line) and the cloze reduced to the two staged blanks (apan connector, magdali form).

Sauna mopalit / karon magluto contrast is idiomatic; recall, chunks, trophy example fine. youTwo opens with 'Usahay' and clozes it as the frequency choice, but usahay is staged productive only in lessons 4-6 and is L4's trophy; rewritten with the staged 'Sauna ... lang' frame (friend scene) keeping magluto as form blank and adding a lexical choice blank on dali.

youOne exactly 16 words, sagad placement and 'maglakaw na ko' cluster correct. Them-line 2 'Unsa na lang kalayo' reads as 'what fire' (kalayo = fire); the degree reading needs the linker 'ka layo'. 'matag buntag' in youTwo echoes the them-line; noted as slightly ahead of the 7-10 staging but acceptable as echo.

Usahay/kasagaran contrast, 'mopahulay lang ko' clitic order and inclusive/exclusive forms are correct; cloze foils are impossible in slot (Matag/Gikan/Ngano before a verb); recall and transfer example fine. No edits.

'Sauna permi ko magtrabaho sa gabii' models permi before the verb correctly; makatulog na ko og walo ka oras is natural. Trophy example 'permi ko gabii makauli' has an unnatural word order (time word wedged between clitic and verb); corrected to 'permi ko makauli og gabii'.

Batasan nako sauna nga + mokaon is the staged structure; 'wala na ko magmeryenda' is correct negated habit and is demanded by the beat (dropped habit) even though staging lists wala na for 7-10; accepted as beat-driven early appearance. youTwo 'Karon moinom lang ko' and cloze cue resolve the niinom foil. No edits.

Naandan na nako ang kainit with mao nga + makalakaw na ko is idiomatic; youTwo 'Sauna magpabilin ko sa sulod matag hapon' licenses the German Präteritum via sauna; form and choice blanks sound. No edits.
Matag buntag taught in the staged block; 'yoga na ang akong ehersisyo' nominal predicate with na is natural; Makahimo ko niini ... bisan gamay ra is correct; gym as speech token acceptable. No edits.

Daghan na ang nausab / mas daghan na ang sakyanan is natural and inclusive 'atong' fits the barber scene. Them-line 2 'imong gimingaw' is not the idiomatic object form for 'what do you miss'; corrected to 'imong gimingawan sa una'. Learner 'Gimingaw ko sa hilom nga plasa diin magdula mi sauna' is fine.

Lahi na / pareho gihapon contrast correct; youTwo 'Wala na mi magsayaw' is the staged wala na + mag- habit, but nothing in lessons 7-10 models wala na + mag- before this typed form blank. Added a distinct third pattern example carrying 'wala na mi maglangoy' so the cloze has an in-block transfer model.

Friend/kitchen beat correct; 'Sauna magluto lang ko og itlog' with completed-vs-habitual form blank disambiguated by the visible cue; foils for Sauna and dali are ungrammatical in slot. 'nausab' in the opening is recognition exposure of a later trophy but natural priming, not a spoiler card.

Commute beat and 'ka layo' fix are in place; youOne is exactly 16 words. youTwo still makes the learner produce and cloze 'matag buntag' in block 1-3 where kada/matag + time unit is not yet productive; rewritten within the block's set (karon + present).

Weekend beat fine, usahay/kasagaran contrast is honest variation after sagad. The companion 'ang akong silingan' is said to the neighbour who is asking, which reads as possibly meaning the listener; concrete referent supplied.

Host/night-shift beat and permi placement before verb are correct in youOne; trophy example order fixed. youTwo again produces 'matag gabii' ahead of stage; rewritten to practise the block's own 'permi ... before verb' with the same ability verb and contextually impossible foils.

Dropped-habit beat matches; batasan nako nga is modelled. youOne has the learner produce 'wala na ko magmeryenda' (L7-10 productive 'wala na + habit') in block 4-6, and the block's 'naandan na nako' is never modelled before L7; both resolved by rewriting the second clause with the already productive gi- form and adding a naandan transfer model.
Tutor/heat beat correct; naandan na nako and mao nga are idiomatic; matag hapon in youTwo is in-block; cloze cue 'recurring actor action' excludes gipabilin; chunks, recall and caption verify.

Cousin/gym-vs-yoga beat correct; cloze on present ability + size is a natural reply to 'why yoga' (bisan slot is open against kung, so correctly not blanked). Speech token 'gym' is an English-spelled loanword without Cebuano orthography; replaced by ehersisyo from the same reply.
Barber beat correct; 'gimingawan' fix applied and 'Gimingaw ko sa' answer is idiomatic; inclusive 'atong lungsod' is right for a local barber. Cloze foils and recall fallbacks are impossible in slot.

Elder/fiesta beat correct; pareho gihapon in the learner line is recycled A2 gihapon required by the beat, so not a staging breach. Speech trio lahi/musika/pareho lacks a connector/aspect word; the typed form blank 'magsayaw' would unjustly reject native 'mosayaw' after wala na; recall foil 'porma' is a plausible answer. All three fixed.

lessonsRead.observation: Grandmother/elder scene, full sentences, no slang. youOne (14 words) carries trophy sauna and tokens sauna/mokaon/lugaw; youTwo 'Ganahan gihapon ko, apan magdali ko sa trabaho inig buntag' (10 words) answers the complication. Cloze: apan as choice (gikan sa/tungod sa/sulod sa impossible before a verb) plus cued form magdali; apan is correctly a choice, not a typed connector, because typed 'pero' would be unjustly rejected (spec forbids apan/pero as competing options). gihapon is the recycled A2 item named in the outline's recycles, so learner-side 'Ganahan gihapon ko' is permitted; the independentFinal HIGH on it is not upheld. DE/EN match. No edit.

Friend scene (lang allowed). youOne contrasts mopalit/magluto with trophy karon; transfer 'Sauna moinom ko og kape, apan karon moinom ko og tsa' is distinct. youTwo 'Sauna magluto lang ko og itlog kay dali ra kini maandam' stays inside block 1-3 (sauna + mag- habitual); cloze = Sauna choice (Ngano/Kinsa/Asa impossible without nga/question frame), cued form magluto, cue-free lexical choice dali. Chunks join exactly; recall foils impossible. nausab in the them-line is recognition exposure only. No edit.

Coworker commute: youOne (16 words) with sagad/mosakay/maglakaw; them-line 2 asks distance; youTwo answers with 'usa na lang ka kilometro'. The cloze tests only Karon and kilometro: it is the one lesson whose exercise contains no verb at all, so the outline's mandated habitual/completed form role is absent (not pedagogically equivalent). The reply can carry it without new errors by using the lesson's own taught verb maglakaw; required rewrite below keeps meaning, 11 words, same DE/EN.

Neighbour scene; companion is now ig-agaw, so listener and companion are distinct. youTwo 'Usahay mouban ang akong ig-agaw kung wala siyay trabaho' (9 words); cloze = Usahay choice (Matag/Ngano/Gikan ungrammatical before a verb) + cued form mouban; frequency and form roles present, the kung clause is a fixed contextual frame. kasagaran vs sagad is honest variation. No edit.

Host scene, no slang. youOne 'Sauna permi ko magtrabaho sa gabii...' practises block 4-6 permi before the verb; youTwo 'Oo, permi na ko makatulog og walo ka oras sa gabii' (11 words). Cloze = permi choice (gikan/kinsa/matag impossible) + makatulog as choice: a typed form here would unjustly reject the colloquial abilitative 'katulog', so choice with contextually impossible foils (stand/speak/move for eight hours after a sleep question) is the correct kind. Frequency and verb roles both present. No edit.

Friend scene. youOne uses batasan nako sauna nga + productive gi- (gibiyaan), no premature 'wala na ko mag-'; third transfer 'Naandan na nako ang tsa inig gabii' supplies the block 4-6 naandan model before L7. youTwo 'Karon moinom lang ko og init nga tsa sa kusina' (10 words); cloze = Karon choice + cued form moinom. Terms, chunks, recall coupled. No edit.

Tutor scene. youOne with naandan/kainit/makalakaw; youTwo 'Sauna magpabilin ko sa sulod matag hapon kay init kaayo' (10 words) is inside block 7-10 (matag productive). Cloze = cued form magpabilin (pagpabilin/ipabilin/gipabilin impossible after Sauna ... ko) + matag choice; the printed 'Sauna ' is a legitimate visible piece of the frame since a typed sauna slot would reject the recycled synonym kaniadto. No edit.

Cousin scene. The them-line 'Unsa man ang imong rutina sa una nimong balay?' says 'at your first house' (una is the ordinal), while DE/EN say 'früheren Wohnung / old place'; source and translations diverge. Required fix to 'sa daan nimong balay' (parallel to L5 'daan nimong trabaho'), propagated through both captions by one replaceText. youTwo 'Makahimo ko niini sa balay bisan gamay ra ang akong oras' answers 'why yoga'; the cloze tests a cued ability form and 'gamay ra ang akong oras' (little time, not garment size) with impossible foils; this is a valid reason reply, not an error, and the counterpart's reading of gamay is rejected.

Barber scene; 'atong lungsod' is genuinely inclusive. youOne (15 words) with daghan/nausab/lungsod (nausab carries na- aspect); them-line now uses idiomatic gimingawan; youTwo 'Gimingaw ko sa hilom nga plasa diin magdula mi sauna' (10 words).
